fp.no_impact: No impact data here (devices may not record it when slow or walking)
map.failed: The map component (Leaflet) failed to load, so the route can't be shown.
mapchart.tip: Hover the route, the chart beside it or this activity's other time / distance charts: every chart and the map mark the same moment (tap on a phone)
mapchart.aria: This activity's elevation, heart rate, power, pace and grade over time or distance, synced with the map
mapchart.none: Pick the metrics to show with the buttons above
mapchart.bands: Elevation shade = grade (up or down alike)
trail_only: The charts on this page apply only to trail runs and hikes.
climbmap.aria: Elevation profile (x = distance) with VAM, heart rate, power or GAP below it; {n} climbs shaded, synced with the map
climbmap.tip:
Map: the line is coloured by grade by default; switch to heart rate, power or one colour (remembered for this page).
Profile: x = distance (km); top = elevation (smoothed); pick VAM (metres climbed per hour, 60-s rolling, estimate), heart rate, power or GAP (grade-adjusted pace) with the buttons; ①② = climbs (≥ 80 m of continuous gain at ≥ 3%).
Sync: hover the profile and the map marks the same spot; hover the route on the map and the profile follows (tap on a phone).
Click a climb on the profile, a row of the table or that stretch of the route: it's outlined on the map; click it again or anywhere else to clear.
climbmap.t_ascent_tip: The whole activity's ascent (its total climbing). The line below is the number of climbs and their gain; a climb = ≥ 80 m of continuous gain at ≥ 3%.
climbmap.t_time_tip: The climbs' moving time, and its share of the activity's moving time.
climbmap.t_vam_tip: The climbs' total gain ÷ the time climbing (metres per hour). "Run %" = the share of climbing time at a cadence ≥ 130 spm; not shown without cadence.
climbmap.t_hr_tip: Heartbeats per 100 m climbed (the median over the climbs); lower = more economical. The comparison with your usual is in the verdict above.
climbmap.vs_help: VAM and beats per 100 m against your recent climbs of a similar grade: ▲▼ = outside your usual middle 50% (the number = how far above / below the median), ≈ = within it. Higher VAM = climbing faster; fewer beats per 100 m = more economical.
climbmap.vs_title: Usual = the median of climbs within ±{pp} pp of grade over the last {weeks} weeks ({n} climbs, estimate): VAM {vam} m/h · beats per 100 m {hr}
climbmap.vs_title_none: Only {n} past climbs of a similar grade (±{pp} pp) (< 5): not compared
pole.summary: In this period: {w} activities with poles, {wo} without (trail runs and hikes); each point is a median, n < {n} isn't drawn. Trail runs and hikes marked in the last 365 days: {year_w} with poles, {year_wo} without.
pole.aria: {metric}: median with and without poles per grade
pole.no_impact: These activities have no impact data (a watch or Stryd may not record it when walking), so downhill compares only vertical speed and cadence.
